6 KPIs¶

In [14]:
# 1. Total Revenue
total_revenue = fact_orders["Revenue"].sum()

# 2. Gross Profit
gross_profit = (
    fact_orders["Revenue"].sum()
    - fact_orders["COGS"].sum()
)

# 3. Gross Margin %
gross_margin = (gross_profit / total_revenue) * 100

# 4. Total Orders
total_orders = fact_orders["Order_ID"].nunique()

# 5. On-Time Delivery %
on_time_delivery = (
    fact_orders["Delivery_Status"]
    .str.lower()
    .eq("on-time")
    .mean()
) * 100

# 6. Fill Rate %
fill_rate = fact_orders["Fill_Rate_Pct"].mean()

print("Total Revenue:", round(total_revenue, 2))
print("Gross Profit:", round(gross_profit, 2))
print("Gross Margin %:", round(gross_margin, 2))
print("Total Orders:", total_orders)
print("On-Time Delivery %:", round(on_time_delivery, 2))
print("Fill Rate %:", round(fill_rate, 2))

Total Revenue: 193992800.65
Gross Profit: 70160851.25
Gross Margin %: 36.17
Total Orders: 12000

Order Quantity Distribution¶

In [17]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

counts, bins, patches = plt.hist(
    fact_orders["Order_Quantity"],
    bins=20,
    edgecolor="black"
)

# Add values on bars
for count, patch in zip(counts, patches):
    if count > 0:
        plt.text(
            patch.get_x() + patch.get_width() / 2,
            count,
            f"{int(count)}",
            ha="center",
            va="bottom",
            fontsize=9
        )

plt.title("Order Quantity Distribution")
plt.xlabel("Order Quantity")
plt.ylabel("Frequency")
plt.tight_layout()

plt.show()

Order Quantity vs Revenue¶

In [22]:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = fact_orders["Order_Quantity"]
y = fact_orders["Revenue"]

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

plt.scatter(
    x,
    y,
    color="steelblue",
    alpha=0.6,
    edgecolor="black"
)

# Trend line
z = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)
p = np.poly1d(z)

plt.plot(
    x,
    p(x),
    color="red",
    linewidth=2
)

plt.title("Order Quantity vs Revenue")
plt.xlabel("Order Quantity")
plt.ylabel("Revenue")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Statistical Analysis Dashboard¶

In [25]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 11))

# ─────────────────────────────────────
# 1. Order Quantity Distribution
# ─────────────────────────────────────
ax = axes[0, 0]

counts, bins, patches = ax.hist(
    fact_orders["Order_Quantity"],
    bins=20,
    color="steelblue",
    edgecolor="black",
    alpha=0.8
)

for count, patch in zip(counts, patches):
    if count > 0:
        ax.text(
            patch.get_x() + patch.get_width() / 2,
            count,
            f"{int(count)}",
            ha="center",
            va="bottom",
            fontsize=8
        )

ax.set_title("Order Quantity Distribution", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")
ax.set_xlabel("Order Quantity")
ax.set_ylabel("Frequency")


# ─────────────────────────────────────
# 2. Revenue Distribution
# ─────────────────────────────────────
ax = axes[0, 1]

counts, bins, patches = ax.hist(
    fact_orders["Revenue"],
    bins=20,
    color="steelblue",
    edgecolor="black",
    alpha=0.8
)

for count, patch in zip(counts, patches):
    if count > 0:
        ax.text(
            patch.get_x() + patch.get_width() / 2,
            count,
            f"{int(count)}",
            ha="center",
            va="bottom",
            fontsize=8
        )

ax.set_title("Revenue Distribution", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")
ax.set_xlabel("Revenue")
ax.set_ylabel("Frequency")


# ─────────────────────────────────────
# 3. Order Quantity vs Revenue
# ─────────────────────────────────────
ax = axes[1, 0]

x = fact_orders["Order_Quantity"]
y = fact_orders["Revenue"]

ax.scatter(
    x,
    y,
    color="steelblue",
    alpha=0.5,
    edgecolor="black"
)

z = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)
p = np.poly1d(z)

ax.plot(x, p(x), color="red", linewidth=2)

ax.set_title("Order Quantity vs Revenue", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")
ax.set_xlabel("Order Quantity")
ax.set_ylabel("Revenue")


# ─────────────────────────────────────
# 4. Processing Days vs Transit Days
# ─────────────────────────────────────
ax = axes[1, 1]

x = fact_orders["Processing_Days"]
y = fact_orders["Transit_Days"]

ax.scatter(
    x,
    y,
    color="steelblue",
    alpha=0.5,
    edgecolor="black"
)

z = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)
p = np.poly1d(z)

ax.plot(x, p(x), color="red", linewidth=2)

ax.set_title(
    "Processing Days vs Transit Days",
    fontsize=14,
    fontweight="bold"
)
ax.set_xlabel("Processing Days")
ax.set_ylabel("Transit Days")


# Overall title
fig.suptitle(
    "Supply Chain Statistical Analysis",
    fontsize=18,
    fontweight="bold"
)

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])
plt.show()

Key Insights¶

In [ ]:
- Revenue and profitability are strong, with **193.99M revenue** and **36.17% gross margin**.
- **On-time delivery is 66.03%**, indicating a major delivery performance issue.
- **Fill rate is 96.78%**, showing strong order fulfillment.
- Revenue is highly skewed, with a small number of high-value orders.
- Order quantity has a positive relationship with revenue.
- Processing time has a weak relationship with transit time.

Recommendations¶

In [ ]:
- Improve on-time delivery by analyzing **carriers and shipping modes**.
- Prioritize fulfillment of **high-value orders**.
- Optimize transportation and carrier performance.
- Maintain the strong **96.78% fill rate** through inventory planning.
- Monitor high-volume products for better demand planning.
